caption: The drawing shows a rectangular piece of textile with a woven or tapestry-like appearance, featuring an intricate pattern of floral and leaf motifs. The design is executed in shades of dark blue and a light beige or off-white color. The main section of the textile is filled with a symmetrical arrangement of large, stylized flowers and leaves interspersed with smaller floral elements. The background consists of densely patterned, small, dot-like marks that create a textured effect behind the larger motifs. Along the lower edge of the textile is a horizontal border that contains a repeated sequence of flowers and leaves in the same color scheme, separated from the central section by a straight, horizontal line. The upper and right edges appear uneven and slightly frayed. The textile is set against a plain, pale background. In the bottom right corner of the drawing, the name "Edmond R. Loris" is written.
title: Woolen Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
